scope: Methods/full text and official author-code inspection only; no datasets downloaded, no training, no C4 access.

items.title: NatLabRockies interpretable_battery_life preprocessing code
read_evidence: 01_process_data.py lines 24-100: reads per-cell RPT/Cycling JSON and parses start/stop, raw QV timestamps as numpy datetimes.
01_process_data.py lines 101-177 and 224-279: extracts RPT/cycling timestamps, charge/discharge capacities, current means, voltage extrema, CV time, and C-rates.
01_process_data.py lines 203-223 and 280-285: synthetic timestamp fills and fixed 10-hour C/5 assumption; unsuitable as true measurement arrival timestamps.

01_process_data.py lines 286-345: EFC from throughput divided by RPT0 charge+discharge capacity; summary features Time_days, Equivalent_Full_Cycles, Capacity_Charge/Discharge, C_rate_Charge/Discharge, Voltage_Max/Min, CV_Time, Label.
01_process_data.py lines 347-409, 410-469, 508-533: spline Q(V), dQ/dV, reciprocal dV/dQ; DeltaV-vs-SOC and derivative; 1000-point grids, clipping behavior, storage keys.
02_extract_features_raw_curves.py lines 8-74 and 76-145: RPT0-normalized capacity, first under-80% targets, week-3 minus week-0 curve features, curve grids.
03_extract_cycling_protocol.py lines 8-53: median cycling C-rates, week-1 DoD relative to RPT0 capacity, square-root C-rate x DoD stress features.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Feature recipe is reproducible; not an ablation study itself. Uses regular weekly early RPT contrasts and observed source code has synthetic timestamp filling.
items.overlap: Supplies actual operational signals and RPT diagnostics that can inform candidate A, but its life targets and retrospective early features are not dynamic online conditional RUL.
unverified: Raw tester acquisition/calibration before these JSON files.
Whether every generated/fill timestamp corresponds to an actual event; code explicitly fabricates some times.

items.title: Predicting Battery Lifetime Under Varying Usage Conditions from Early Aging Data
read_evidence: HTML sections 2.1-2.4 and 3.3-3.9; equations (2)-(5) include elastic-net log-lifetime regression and hierarchical Bayesian regression.
Section 2.2 lines 115-128: var(DeltaQ) lifetime correlation -0.686; optimized mean Delta dQ/dV over 3.60-3.90V correlation -0.848.
Section 2.3 lines 133-147: group-level split; DoD >=40% train/high-DoD test, DoD <40% OOD test; repeated five-fold CV, feature forward selection and 2 vs 3 feature comparison.

Section 2.4 lines 149-159 and Table 2: dummy, cycling-condition, discharge-feature, elastic-net and HBM comparison. 3-feature elastic-net MAPE 15.1% high-DoD and 33.0% low-DoD; 2-feature HBM 16.9%/21.8%.
Supplementary lines 406-412: week-4 RPT omitted for test error; one-week RPT intervals give higher errors; suggests at least 2-week interval needed for early degradation-rate features.
Experimental procedures: 225 NMC/Gr 250mAh; weekly C/2 and C/5 RPT; 80% rated capacity EOL; early total-lifetime endpoint, not rolling dynamic RUL.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Features and model variants are compared; feature count 2 vs 3, condition-only vs cell-level, in-distribution vs low-DoD extrapolation, and RPT interval sensitivity are explicitly reported.
items.overlap: Early operation conditions plus measured cell-health signals predicting lifetime is established; signals-driven candidate must target online as-of updating or different event/time semantics.

items.title: EntroLnn: Entropy-Guided Liquid Neural Networks for Operando Refinement of Battery Capacity Fade Trajectories
read_evidence: Section 2.1 equations (1)-(6): temperature/spatial entropy; lumped thermal model; online thermal coefficient adaptation by gradient update.

Section 2.2 equation (7) and Section 2.3 equations (9)-(16): five entropy feature embeddings/attention; 64-D initial LNN state; d h/dt = -alpha*h + tanh(W_h h + averaged input); online gradient update and value+slope matching losses.
Section 3: MIT-Stanford 124 LFP battery dataset; Bat003 reference; initial first 100 cycles; dynamic LNN uses sliding windows about 100 cycles.
Sections 4.2-4.3: 0.004577 SoH MAE and 18-cycle EOL MAE with 10% data, 123 target batteries excluding reference; long-term CFT MAE about 0.0045.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Compares proposed method to BFRN, BTL, DRRN, TLPH, DCNN; evaluates entropy features and single temperature feature. Full independent EOL/FPT interval calibration is not demonstrated in read sections.
items.overlap: Continuous-time LNN, online thermal/SoH features, and CFT refinement overlap strongly with candidate A's generic continuous latent propagation; candidate must encode actual irregular diagnostic arrival semantics and not just use ODE.
unverified: RUL distribution calibration and interval-censoring event likelihood were not identified in the full text sections read.

items.title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Two-Phase Hybrid Deteriorating Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Wiener Process
read_evidence: IEEE Access article sections II and III and conclusion; equations (2)-(3) explicitly define lifetime and as-of RUL as first-passage times over threshold.

Methods: two-phase linear/nonlinear Wiener hybrid; random heterogeneity, change time and degradation state at the change point; EM/profile likelihood offline identification and Bayes-rule online updating when new observation becomes available.
Evaluation: numerical simulation plus practical lithium-ion case; compares two-phase hybrid against two-phase linear and single-phase nonlinear alternatives; reports MSE, AE, RE and TMSE.
Conclusion explicitly assumes perfect degradation measurements and identifies real measurement variability as future work.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Model-family comparison and simulated/practical evaluation are present; real sparse scheduled RPT arrival handling and missing-inspection interval censoring were not located in read article sections.
items.overlap: Strongest direct overlap for probabilistic FPT RUL, two-stage stochastic degradation, and Bayesian updates after new battery observations.
unverified: Whether model experiment schedules are equivalent to UConn/ISU RPT schedule.
Whether reported online updates assume every observation time is exact and complete beyond the perfect-measurement statement.

items.title: An interpretable online prediction method for remaining useful life of lithium-ion batteries
read_evidence: Methods Section II and equations including (26): CC charge, CV charge, CC discharge and temperature health indicators; SVR predicts HIs, GPR predicts capacity; SHAP groups HIs at >50% contribution threshold; Gaussian non-white noise is added to state variables for capacity regeneration; UKF modifies HIs/noise.
Equation (26): Cap3 = Cap2 + Nhat; Cap2 used for lower confidence bound and Cap3 for regeneration-sensitive upper bound.

Experiments: NASA B5, B6, B7; starts T=70/80/90 cycles; rated 2Ah, EOL 1.4Ah with B7 special threshold 1.5Ah; comparison M1 against models without this framework; AE<5 and narrowest reported CI about 2.
Author conclusion notes predicted endpoint deviation because GPR capacity prediction is also used as UKF observation, constraining capacity/CI accuracy.
items.protocol_or_ablation: M1/M2 comparisons over three starting prefixes; the principal novelty test concerns regeneration-aware interval upper bound. No source scheduled RPT interval-censoring likelihood is described in inspected sections.
items.overlap: Online HI trajectory prediction, filtering, capacity regeneration and RUL thresholding are already combined; materially overlaps A and the path/regeneration portion of B.
unverified: Search and official full-text snippets supplied method details; PDF endpoint was not accessible directly through web fetch.
No demonstrated right/interval-censoring likelihood for source-observed threshold crossing in inspected content.

items.title: Dynamic survival analysis via a landmarking-gradient boosting approach and its application to kidney transplant data
read_evidence: Methods section 'Dynamic prediction', equation (1): survival from landmark s through s+w conditional on survival through s and longitudinal history y_i(s), X_i.
LGBM algorithm section equations (residual gradient, tree update, line search) and Brier-score equation; simulation equations (6)-(9) link longitudinal mixed effects to survival hazard.

Experiments: linear and nonlinear settings, sample sizes 300/650/1000/1500, censoring 30/50/90%, varying landmark time; linear setting favors correctly specified joint model, nonlinear larger/high-censoring/later landmark settings favor LGBM.
Real application compares LMM vs LOCF and joint/Cox landmark/LGBM; two-fold CV repeated 100 times, LMM imputation gives better AUC/Brier than LOCF.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Includes imputation comparison and simulation conditions designed to test model misspecification and censoring; landmark updates are predefined risk sets, not irregular streaming RPT arrivals.
items.overlap: Shows longitudinally updated conditional survival prediction and observation/censoring semantics are standard. It is non-battery and does not model continuous latent degradation FPT.

items.title: Joint model for longitudinal and spatio-temporal survival data
read_evidence: Sections 2.1-2.3, equations (1)-(6): shared random effect links longitudinal and discrete survival processes; conditional independence of the two processes given random effects is stated at Eq. (6); INLA estimation and cross-validated dynamic conditional likelihood are described.
Empirical evaluation: 57,258 mortgage loans and 2,559,056 observations, 16,239 prepayment events; compare base joint, spatial main-effect and spatio-temporal interaction model at six forecast times.
Results: spatial main effects improve the joint model consistently, interaction improvement is less clear.
items.protocol_or_ablation: Joint-model variants isolate spatial effects and interactions; time is discrete monthly and application is mortgage event prediction.
items.overlap: A shared latent state/covariate association with event hazard is established general joint-model structure; a battery contribution must address continuous first passage plus irregular RPT inspection intervals rather than shared latent variables alone.
unverified: arXiv v1 posted 2023; not a 2024-2026 battery method, used only as general methodological prior.

new_mechanism_assessment.candidate_A: Continuous state propagation driven by high-rate current/voltage/temperature/throughput, with updates only when a real RPT diagnostic measurement arrives, remains a plausible but unproven distinction. Generic ODE/LNN + filtering/Bayesian update is already covered across EntroLnn, two-phase Wiener, and online UKF regeneration work.
new_mechanism_assessment.candidate_B: Source-observed first threshold RPT time is exactly the RPT stop time, not interval-censored. Interval censoring applies only to a distinct latent continuous physical first-passage estimand under explicit path, monotonicity/regeneration, measurement-error, and follow-up assumptions. With capacity rebound, last-above/first-below endpoints do not bound the first crossing because an earlier crossing may recover. Do not claim this as novelty without changing and naming the estimand.
new_mechanism_assessment.source_event_open_question: No read battery paper was found that explicitly combines actual irregular RPT arrivals with as-of updates for the precisely defined source-observed event; event time is the threshold-crossing RPT stop, not interval-censored. Search coverage does not prove none exists.
new_mechanism_assessment.paper_identity_correction: Li et al. 2024 Cell Reports Physical Science 10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101891 is not Gasper et al. NREL Physical interpretation of early battery life prediction models (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14285817); they are distinct papers related to ISU-ILCC NMC/Gr.
